notes: WITH SKILL: pass rate 100% ± 0% across ALL 9 runs — perfectly deterministic output regardless of run
WITHOUT SKILL: pass rate 42% ± 16% — significant variance driven mainly by Eval 1 (0.22–0.33 range)
Eval 1 (split hypotheses) shows the largest delta (+0.74): baseline NEVER splits interventions across all 3 runs, skill ALWAYS does
Eval 3 (forced numbers) shows smallest delta (+0.39): even without skill the model flags 30% as unrealistic — this assertion is partially non-discriminating
WITHOUT SKILL time variance is high (stddev=30.4s): run1 took 100s (went into full experiment design), run2-3 took 10-22s (short outputs) — scope creep is inconsistent
Skill adds ~3160 tokens on average (+13%) — cost of reading SKILL.md — but eliminates all output variance and scope creep
Assertion 'Confidence level explicitly stated as provisional' is highly discriminating for Eval 2-3: baseline never uses the label, skill always does
Assertion 'No fabricated quantitative impact numbers' is highly discriminating for Eval 2: baseline fabricates concrete targets (30s, 40%, 15 NPS) in 2/3 runs
